issues.legal_issue: A father’s attestation of a sale deed executed by the mother does not make the sale a transaction by the father as natural guardian when he was alive and involved in the minor’s affairs.
material_facts: The mother executed the sale of the minors’ land while acting as their guardian, and the father attested the deed.
There was no evidence that the father had ceased taking an interest in the minors’ affairs or that they were in the mother’s care to the exclusion of the father.
The father’s attestation showed that he was present and involved.
issues.conclusion: The mother’s sale could not be treated as a sale by the father and natural guardian merely because the father attested the deed.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956, the father is the natural guardian while alive; the mother may be treated as guardian in the father’s place in exceptional circumstances where he is effectively absent from the child’s affairs. In Jijabai Vithalrao Gajre v. Pathankhan, AIR 1971 SC 315, the father had lived separately and taken no interest in the minor, so the mother could act as guardian; those circumstances were not established here.

rule.if: minor_property_sale_dispute and mother_executed_sale and father_attested_deed and father_remained_involved

predicates.minor_property_sale_dispute: The dispute concerns a sale of property belonging to a person who was a minor when the sale was made.
predicates.mother_executed_sale: The minor’s mother executed the sale deed while purporting to act as guardian.
predicates.father_attested_deed: The minor’s father attested the sale deed executed by the mother.
predicates.father_remained_involved: The father was alive and the evidence did not show that he had stopped taking an interest in the minor’s affairs.

issues.definition: When a minor’s property-sale dispute involves a sale deed executed by the mother and attested by a father who remained involved in the minor’s affairs, the sale is not treated as the father’s transaction as natural guardian.

issues.legal_issue: A sale of a minor’s immovable property executed by the mother without authority as natural guardian is void, rather than merely voidable, where the father remained present and involved and court permission was not obtained.
material_facts: The mother sold the respondents’ land while they were minors, and the father attested the sale deed.
The father was present and involved; there was no evidence that he had ceased taking an interest in the minors’ affairs.
The sale was made without permission of the court.
The trial court found no reliable evidence that the sale was for legal necessity or for the minors’ benefit.
The respondents sued for possession after attaining majority, and the suit was held to be in time.
issues.conclusion: The sale was void, not merely voidable, and the challenge to the suit on the ground that it was time-barred because the sale was only voidable failed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 8 of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 permits a legal guardian to alienate a minor’s immovable property only for necessity or the benefit of the minor or the minor’s estate and after obtaining the court’s prior permission. An alienation by a legal guardian without the required permission is described as voidable at the minor’s instance; here, however, the mother’s execution was not a sale by the father as natural guardian. Section 8 is intended to protect a minor’s property even from a parent’s depredations. The Court distinguished Jijabai Vithalrao Gajre v. Pathankhan, AIR 1971 SC 315, where the father was effectively absent from the minor’s affairs.

predicates.possession_suit_after_minor_reaches_majo: A person who owned property as a minor brings a suit for possession after attaining majority.
predicates.mother_sold_minor_property_without_guard: The mother executed the sale of the minor’s property, while the father was alive and involved and the mother was not acting in his place as natural guardian.
predicates.court_permission_absent: The sale of the minor’s immovable property was made without prior permission of the court.

issues.definition: When a possession suit is brought after the owner reaches majority and the mother sold the minor’s property without authority as guardian and without prior court permission, the sale is void.
